icp: Instagram-first course creators, coaches, newsletter operators, and digital-product sellers using one professional account
pain: Creators miss high-intent comment leads or pay contact-based automation fees for a broad chatbot suite they do not need
revenueHypothesis: Creators will pay GBP 19 monthly or GBP 190 annually for CommentShift when signup, Instagram connection, comment-to-DM delivery, tracked links, and billing work as one hosted service
mvpAcceptance: Railway production contains healthy PostgreSQL, Redis, and one continuously running delivery worker
Vercel production has the matching database, Redis, encryption, authentication, Resend, Meta, and Stripe configuration without secret exposure
All Prisma migrations are deployed to the production PostgreSQL database
The commercial UI is branded CommentShift while the MIT-licensed OpenReply repository and engine attribution remain intact
A visitor can sign up through a delivered Resend magic link and reach an authenticated workspace
A Meta tester can connect one Instagram professional account and a real keyword comment creates a sent private reply
The private reply contains a tracked link whose click is recorded
Stripe test checkout completes and its signed webhook changes the workspace subscription state
The existing application tests, lint, typecheck, Prisma generation, and production build remain green
GitHub Actions and a Vercel READY deployment are bound to the delivered commit
rollback: Revert the scoped OpenReply Cloud launch commit, restore the previous Prisma schema through a forward migration, and promote the last verified Vercel deployment.
stopConditions: Stop on secret exposure, target ambiguity, duplicate product work, three failed attempts, or a failed rollback check.
Stop public customer onboarding until the central Meta app has the required business verification and Advanced Access permissions.
Stop production billing activation if Stripe products, webhook signing secret, or live-mode account ownership cannot be verified.
